result:
If I could change the world in one way—truly, irrevocably—I would instill in every human being an unshakable, visceral understanding that their well-being is inextricably bound to the well-being of others and the living world around them.

Not as a moral suggestion or a noble idea, but as a felt truth—like knowing you’re bleeding when you’re cut, or feeling hunger when you haven’t eaten. This wouldn’t erase all conflict or suffering, but it would dissolve the illusion of separateness that fuels greed, hatred, exploitation, and ecological destruction. Compassion wouldn’t be a virtue to aspire to; it would be as instinctive as breath.

In that world, we’d still stumble, argue, and make mistakes—but we’d do so as members of a shared body, tending to each other not out of duty, but because harming another would feel like harming oneself. And perhaps then, we’d finally grow up.
